issues.description: SigningMode-to-bytes dispatch is duplicated between sign_message and verify_signature.
issues.detail: The same mode-to-bytes mapping is reimplemented as parallel if/elif ladders in both sign_message and verify_signature inside the new signing.py. Extract a single private _message_to_bytes(mode, message) helper so the next CHIP mode is added in one place and the two functions cannot silently disagree.

issues.description: signing_mode_enum exists as both a free function and properties, with a coincidental fall-through default.
issues.detail: wallet_request_types.py defines a module-level signing_mode_enum and two property wrappers that just delegate to it — two names, one behavior. The function also enumerates three of four (is_hex, safe_mode) combos and falls through to CHIP_0002 for the last. Pick one home and spell out the fourth branch explicitly (or use a dict/match).

issues.description: verify_signature in the new util returns the RPC VerifySignatureResponse, leaking the wire schema into the library.
issues.detail: chia/wallet/util/signing.py imports VerifySignatureResponse from wallet_request_types and returns it directly. The extracted utility should return a small (bool, str|None) or local result struct so non-RPC callers can reuse it — which is the stated motivation for the extraction. Otherwise the util is coupled to RPC schema evolution.

issues.description: verify_signature docstring is stale, still referencing a ':param request:' that no longer exists.
issues.detail: The new signature takes signing_mode, public_key, message, signature, and address as keyword args, but the docstring is a copy-paste artifact from the old RPC method describing a request parameter. Fix or delete it — stale docs on a freshly extracted library function are worse than no docs.

issues.description: convert_secret_key_to_synthetic is an instance method on Wallet that uses no instance state.
issues.detail: It only calls calculate_synthetic_secret_key with a module-level constant, yet RPC callers reach through main_wallet to invoke it for unrelated DID/NFT keys. That conflates synthetic-key derivation with main_wallet identity. Move it to a free function in chia/wallet/util/signing.py (or a staticmethod) where the boundary is honest.

issues.description: DID error message wording drifted during the pure refactor.
issues.detail: Pre-extraction code distinguished 'Missing DID inner puzzle' from 'Invalid inner DID puzzle'; current_p2_puzzle_hash collapses these into a single 'Invalid DID inner puzzle'. Probably harmless, but it is a user-visible string change inside a refactor PR — restore the original wording or call it out in the changelog.

synthesis.summary: The panel agrees this is a well-shaped extraction — three near-duplicate sign_message implementations collapse into one library function, and the wallets are reduced to exposing a puzzle hash. The work stops one step short of the cleanup that motivates it: the SigningMode-to-bytes dispatch is still duplicated inside the new module, signing_mode_enum exists as both a free function and properties with a coincidental fall-through default, and the util leaks the RPC VerifySignatureResponse back into the library. A stale docstring, a misplaced convert_secret_key_to_synthetic on the base Wallet, and a DID error-message wording drift round it out. Needs-work but small and mechanical — fix and land.
